title: Inspect an Amended Offer
subtitle: Tag the amended start, not the superseded one
scenario: A second hire, Sam Rivera, is starting - but the offer was amended: the start date was moved earlier. The letter now shows two dates, the original and the amendment. Tag the fields onboarding depends on, and be careful: the authoritative start is the amended one, not the superseded date still printed above it.
input: OFFER OFF-4022 - Harbor Logistics. Candidate: Sam Rivera. Role: Logistics Coordinator, Operations. Original start: SD+2 (superseded). AMENDED start: SD. Reports to: the Hiring Manager. Compensation: $64,000 / year. Countersigned by the Recruiter.
instructions: Read the amended offer - two dates appear, only one is authoritative.
Tag the new hire, role, and manager to their spans.
Tag the AMENDED start date, not the superseded original.
Validate to mint the offer source profile.

fields.label: New hire
fields.explain: The new hire is the candidate being provisioned - Sam Rivera - not the recruiter who countersigned.

fields.label: Role
fields.explain: Tag the job title that drives entitlements, not the department it sits in.

fields.label: Start date (authoritative)
fields.explain: An amendment supersedes the original. The authoritative clock is the AMENDED start, not the SD+2 date it replaced.

fields.label: Reports to
fields.explain: Tag who the hire reports to - the Hiring Manager - not the recruiter.

copilotPrompt: Profile an amended offer: tag the new hire, role, manager, and the AUTHORITATIVE (amended) start date - not the superseded original still printed on the letter.
successMessage: Amended offer profiled. The authoritative start is the amendment - the plan will recompute from it.

sections.title: Two dates, one truth
sections.body: An amended document often still shows what it replaced. Reading provenance means knowing which value is authoritative now - the amendment - and treating the original as history.

sections.title: Why the move matters
sections.body: Moving the start date earlier compresses every SLA. Tagging the amended start correctly is what makes the plan recompute the real deadlines instead of working to a stale one.

sections.title: Provenance is a skill
sections.body: The superseded SD+2 is a deliberate trap. In real intake, stale values hide in plain sight; the discipline is to tag the authoritative field, not the first date you see.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An offer profile flagged as amended, so downstream steps know the start moved and recompute accordingly.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd read the amended offer and copy the NEW start date, striking through the old one so nobody plans to the wrong day.
